items.title: Jack Teagarden Interview, 1959-10-29
items.q: And then I went with, uh, Benny Pollock. Which at that time had a wonderful band for a big band... There was a little kid with us, uh, the name of Benny Goodman. In those days he was about 18 years old. Jimmy McPartland and, uh, Bud Freeman.

ctx.x: Okay, whenever you're ready. Well, how did you learn trombone and develop your style? That's what I really like to know.

Well, I'll tell you, when I was, uh, pretty young, my mother and I used to play in, uh, the old silent movie theaters. We used to play for the comedies and, uh, I don't know, just trombone and piano. You know, learn more technique because I had the whole, swing the whole thing, melody and all. You know. And, uh, my mother played very good ragtime piano, which was very good for those years. Then, uh, I lost my father in 1918 with the flu. And then I went, we went to Oklahoma City. And I went one more year of, uh,…

Can we back up for a minute and go back to your early period? Yeah. Because there's some particular people I'd like to ask you about some particular things. What kind of training did Peg Kelly have that he should develop this wonderful style?

items.title: 67848_Jimmy McPartland oral history interview
items.q: Jack came with the band... So we had a great small band... Benny Goodman and Jack Teagarden and Jimmy McPartland on the cornet.

ctx.x: Yes. He said I'll be the arranger which was what he was doing anyway, and it will give me more time to arrange and Jack came in on trombone. So we had a small band, see it was eleven, twelve piece band that we had, the Pollack band. He even had a couple of fiddles in there and a cello (shuttle?). At the Park Central Hotel that was. So Jack came with the band, Glen did the arranging and we had a great small band. We used to have the small band come out in front and you know when we played jam numbers, jam you…

But Glen was very graceful about it and bowed out. A funny thing happened though on that Pollack band. The manager, this guy's name was Bernie Foyer. And after we got through the Park Central Hotel we got on tour and we were playing in these theaters and dance halls and so forth. And Benny Goodman, Gil Rodin, Harry Goodman and myself used to room together, most all of the time. We used to play a lot of hand ball. And between shows one day at the Fox Brooklyn Theater we went upstairs on the roof and got a hand…
